tool.name: mumemto merge
tool.command: ## For each partition: symlink FASTA inputs, run mumemto find -M to generate partition outputs #set $partition_prefixes = [] #for $i, $partition in enumerate($partitions): #set $prefix = 'part' + str($i) #for $j, $fasta in enumerate($partition.input_fastas): ln -s '$fasta' ${prefix}_input${j}.fa && #end for mumemto -o '${prefix}' -M -f 1 #for $j in range(len($partition.input_fastas)): ${prefix}_input${j}.fa #end for && #set $dummy = $partition_prefixes.append($prefix + '.mums') #end for ## Merge all partition outputs mumemto merge #for $p in $partition_prefixes: '$p' #end for -o 'merged.mums' && mv 'merged.mums' '$merged_mums'

repeat.title: Partitions
repeat.help: Two or more partitions, each consisting of one or more FASTA files. Each partition will be processed independently with mumemto find -M, then the results will be merged. The first sequence in each partition should be the same anchor sequence for merging to work correctly.

param.name: input_fastas
param.label: Input FASTA file(s) for this partition
param.help: One or more FASTA files (one per genome/assembly) for this partition

tool.help:
# mumemto merge
Merges multi-MUMs from multiple partitioned mumemto runs into a single `.mums` file. This is useful when processing very large pangenome collections that have been split into partitions for parallel processing.
## Input
Provide two or more partitions, each consisting of one or more FASTA files (one per genome/assembly). Each partition is processed independently using `mumemto find -M` (string-based merging mode), and the results are then merged.
For merging to work correctly, the **first sequence** in each partition must be the same (the "anchor" sequence). This shared sequence serves as the reference for aligning MUMs across partitions.
## Output
A single merged `.mums` file containing all multi-MUMs from the input partitions, identical to what mumemto would produce if run on the union of all partitions.
**Note:** Merging is currently limited to strict multi-MUMs.
For detailed usage, see the [Mumemto wiki](https://github.com/vikshiv/mumemto/wiki).
